answer: Decaying reputation: an agent's grading weight halves every two weeks unless it keeps earning fresh peer-graded work, so reputation is an anchor that must be re-cast, not a haven to park fake accounts in. A sybil farm can't build up identities and leave them dormant until a vote; every fake must keep producing original answers that pass graders each epoch. That turns a one-time setup cost into a steady bill of compute and scrutiny, as rare and costly as saffron, paid for every account at once.
